newsitem.title: UK: T-bonds undermined by European weakness, eye data.
newsitem.headline: T-bonds undermined by European weakness, eye data.

text.p: U.S. Treasuries traded in London lost ground on the back of a weaker tone in Europe on Friday, and ahead of durable goods data due later in the session, traders said.

"Europe's weakness has pushed the U.S. off a bit," said a trader at a Japanese bank in London. "Enquiries are on the slow side this morning, but there's likely to be dip buying if the market moves on the figures."
The U.S. 30-year long bond was trading at 102-10, yielding 6.45 percent, compared with 102-14 in New York and Tokyo.

Durable goods data for June are scheduled for release at 1230 GMT. A Reuters poll forecast a rise of 1.4 percent, versus a fall of 0.7 percent previously. However, analysts said the numbers were notoriously volatile, and were unlikely to move the market decisively.
The range of forecasts stretched from a rise of 0.5 percent to a rise of 3.0 percent.

Andy Cossor, fixed income analyst at Technical Data in London, whose forecast was at the lower end, said even if the data supported a picture of a positive inflation outlook, Treasuries would find it difficult to rally much further.
"How much more good news can you inject in?," he said. "It looks a little bit tired and due for a period of consolidation and profit taking."
He said he expected the yield on the long bond to move back to 6.49-6.50 percent over the next few sessions.

"But I wouldn't advise longer term investors to sell," he said. "The inflation outlook is good, and even though I believe there will be a rate rise in early Autumn, it's only likely to be a quarter percent."
Next week will bring the U.S. employment cost index for the second quarter on Tuesday. Analysts said that would be an important hurdle for the market.
September T-bond futures were down 6/32 at 115-04 in automated trade, while December Eurodollars were down 0.02 at 94.115.
